activities.title: Predict the output
activities.prompt: For an active-high, edge-aligned PWM signal in up-count mode, which two actions create the pulse?

options.label: HIGH at TEZ, then LOW at compare
LOW at TEZ, then HIGH at compare
TOGGLE at TEZ and again at compare

activities.explanation: At timer-empty (TEZ) the period begins HIGH. The comparator ends the high interval by switching LOW.

activities.title: Build the signal path
activities.prompt: Put the setup steps in a workable order before enabling the timer.

items.label: Program the generator's timer and compare actions
Create a timer and operator, then connect them
Create a comparator and generator on that operator

activities.explanation: The timer/operator relationship comes first; comparator and generator handles must exist before their event/action table can be configured.

activities.title: Tune a PWM waveform
activities.prompt: Set 1,000 Hz and 25% duty, then predict the HIGH interval in microseconds before checking.
activities.explanation: Period = 1,000,000 / frequency in microseconds. At 1 kHz the period is 1,000 µs; 25% duty means HIGH for 250 µs. The visual is a timing model, not an electrical measurement.

activities.title: Explain the second compare event
activities.prompt: Why can one compare threshold trigger twice during an up-down PWM cycle, and what must an action rule specify?
activities.modelAnswer: The counter crosses the threshold once while counting up and once while counting down. A center-aligned action must include timer direction so the two crossings can apply different output actions.
